entries: The library opened with 766 evaluated players — 553 moving up from FCS, 213 moving down from P4 — across 10 Player Books.
Championship path added: every FBS team's rooms measured against its conference-best standard, with the getable players named and a full class builder.
Estimated NIL projections added to every player page and to the championship path, modelled from reported market bands — not reported deals.
Saved classes: save any player to a school's class from his page, print or email the class (board picture plus full text, Gmail included), and share a class with a link that opens it live.
My Team mode added: pick your school once and player pages, fits and the championship path frame themselves around your rooms.
Every book now carries a verified headshot for every player — 766 of 766.

Targeting layer added: 228 players now carry 'What he does best' tags — 19 archetypes, from vertical-stretch receivers to press corners, computed from their trait stats — with a filter in both directories and on the championship path. Every bio now opens with the player's hometown.

Value Board added: all 683 priced players ranked inside their position by grade against price — a steady lens for what he is now and a ceiling lens for what he could become — with each player's NIL band printed beside his score.

Budget Report added to the championship path: each team's rooms ranked by their gap to the conference standard, the cheapest getable fix in every room, and ready-built classes at $500K, $1M and $2M that open straight into the class builder.

P4 Down book expanded to ten home states: the Florida, Georgia, Tennessee, Oklahoma and South Carolina screen added 246 fully evaluated players, taking the book to 459 — every one graded against the 2026 pool, priced, and carrying a Call, with headshots verified. The site now carries 1,012 evaluated players.

Player lists now show what each man does best: his skill tags sit beside his name in both directories, so a press corner, a YAC threat or a pulling lineman reads at a glance without opening his page. 247 of the 1,012 players carry tags.

Overpay notes added: when a player's projected price outruns his grade by 30 points or more inside his position pool, his page now says 'Priced as an overpay' beside the band, with both percentiles printed, and the Value Board flags him. 174 of the 929 priced players carry the note.

Prospect List added: tap the star beside any player's name in either directory — or the highlight button on his page — and he collects on your Prospect List, one shortlist across both directions with his grade, likely level and NIL band at a glance. Highlight first; pricing stays in a school's saved class. The list saves in this browser.

Class building now names the fall-off: every player saved to a class shows the rotation player he pushes out — the lowest-graded man with real volume in that room — and the grade points gained over him, his row also prints where he slots into the room, and the class totals the points gained over the players replaced. The Budget Report's ready-built classes carry the same figures, and a man who falls off under the class you've built is marked in the full room listing.

Six of our P4 Down players were nationally ranked in the 2026 transfer portal class, and their pages now say so at the top: Isiah Canion (#33 by 247Sports, #51 by ESPN), Carius Curne (#45, #53), Deuce Knight (#100, #92), Malcolm Simmons (#151), Kamauryn Morgan (#176) and Jack Van Dorselaer (#219) — the ranking each list gave them when they moved to their current schools last January.

P4 Down is complete: the final 976 candidates from the all-states screen have now been evaluated, adding 449 players — the P4 Down book covers 908 players across 2,769 pages, every one with his level, The Call, fits, NIL band and a verified headshot. The Value Board now ranks 1,378 players, targeting tags were recomputed across the full pool, and the championship path's getable lists were rebuilt with the new players included.

New Map view: every player in the library is placed by his hometown. Click states on the map — a real map, with Canada drawn in its place as a single region — or tick states from the alphabetical list beside it; map and list stay in sync, several states can be selected together, and the matching players from both books list below. International players have their own globe block, and the eight players whose hometown is not on record are counted openly, never dropped. The championship path now also spells out what Regional means for the school on screen — its home state plus the states that border it.

The upgrade test on the championship path and in the Budget Report now works the way depth actually works: a player counts as an upgrade for a school when his benchmark beats the lowest-graded man with playing time in that room's rotation — the man he would push off the bottom — not only when he beats the room's best man. Players who do beat the best man are badged “Beats your starter”. Rooms whose players all fell short of the volume bars previously named no upgrades at all; they name theirs now too. For ULM, the five rooms that read “No getable fix at any price” — RB, ED, S, LB and DI — now carry 24, 17, 36, 39 and 46 upgrades.

Filter by build and by skill: the directories now filter on height and weight — or on build for his position — and on individual skill traits at a percentile bar you set (pass-rush win rate, yards after catch, ballhawk rate and 26 more). Ticked archetypes can now require ALL of them instead of any, and a Value lean toggle keeps only the players whose trait grade runs at least 30 points ahead of their price.

Limited action, depth fits, a player builder, and a ribbon: a player who flashed in limited action now shows it — his top skills sit at the top of his bio, and a skill produced on a small sample prints in red as Limited action with the sample size beside it (the trait filter can include them, off by default). Fits now run on the depth test everywhere, not just the championship path: a player page lists the rooms where he beats the starter first, then the rooms where he improves the depth, and Fits my team counts both. The new Prototype search builds a player from inputs — position, size (with a one-click optimal size for the position), hometown, archetypes, skill bars, NIL ceiling and eligibility — and returns the matches ready to star or save to a class. And the directory filters now live in a ribbon menu at the top of the page: tabs for Search, Size, Hometown, Archetypes and Skills that stay closed until you open the one you want — Hometown is a new filter, a state list with counts — while the strip always shows the result count, which filter groups are active, and a Clear all.

The path to a championship now works from the bottom of the room up: the lowest man in a room is replaceable whatever his snap count — a player with little or no playing time no longer blocks an upgrade — and the class builder pairs each addition against that bottom man by name. The Hometown filter in the menu now shows your picks on a map as you choose them; press Done and the map folds away with your selection in place.

22. The top of the site is now a real menu bar. Find players opens a menu — both directories, Prototype search, the Map, the Value Board and your Prospect list — and Teams opens one for the Championship path and both comparison pages; What changed sits in the bar too. The little line of text links under each page heading is gone, because the menus carry those routes now, and the page you're on is marked in the menu.

23. The front page is rebuilt: one dark stage under the menu bar, the headline “The portal, evaluated.”, and the library's counts up front — 1,461 players evaluated, 10 Player Books, 138 FBS schools. The two doors into the library sit in the middle (FCS — Moving Up, P4 — Moving Down), your team is one tap away, and the rest of the tools rest in a quiet row underneath.

24. Skills now read the way coaches talk. Every skill shows as a Top X% finish against the other players at his position and his level, with the exact percentile kept small beside it and a one-line plain explanation of what the skill is — “Sack finish: share of his pressures that end in a sack.” Red limited-action skills print their sample in words (“on just 51 snaps”), and the Skills filter panel explains its own bars and counts in plain language.

25. Fits now run in every direction. Every player is fitted against all 138 FBS schools, and each fit is tagged by the move — Up, Lateral or Down — with same-level fits read off his grade exactly as it stands. Every fit also carries its offer: his NIL band where he prices, or Scholarship only where he doesn't — no dollar figure attached, and a scholarship-only addition costs nothing in the class builder or the Budget Report. A new Offer filter in the directories and in Prototype search lets you look by offer type, measured against your team when one is set.

26. The “What he does best” section on each player page now speaks the same plain language as the skills at the top of the page. Every tag carries a one-line plain explanation of what it means, and the numbers behind the tag are written out in words — “Yards after the catch 13.0 per catch · Top 7%” in place of the old shorthand — with percentiles shown as Top X% finishes and “stand-in stat” in place of “proxy”. The tags themselves and every number behind them are unchanged; only the wording moved.

27. Every player is listed now. The full list holds 18,384 players — every graded player in the P4, G6 and FCS. The 1,461 fully evaluated players keep their full pages, with band, fits and The Call. The other 16,923 are standard records: name, school, conference, position, his 2026 grade and his playing time — nothing more is claimed for them, and their pages say so. Find the list under Find players → “Every player — the full list”, or through Prototype search set to Everywhere.

28. The whole site is dark now. Every page — directories, player pages, the Value Board, the championship path — sits on the same near-black design with white type and one accent colour, built to be worked in for hours. The numbers did not change; the light pages are retired.

29. Set “My team” in the top bar and the site takes on your school: its logo appears in the bar and its colour becomes the accent everywhere, over the same black. Clear the team and everything goes back to neutral black — and your saved classes stay saved either way.
